title: Day 70 · Week 10, Day 0 — Body: embryo to fetus — the organ inventory, the window that has mostly closed, the risk curve after a normal scan, and the sickness that peaks before it breaks
summary: The day the embryo becomes a fetus: day 56 after fertilization, the end of Carnegie stage 23, about 30 mm and a few grams, heart at ~180 bpm, milk-tooth buds in the jaw. What the change of name marks (organogenesis ends; growth and maturation begin — a roughly thousand-fold weight gain to term) and a system-by-system inventory: heart, limbs, face, gut and kidneys built in plan; palate and genitals finishing; lungs and brain present and far from done. The teratology windows (all-or-none, embryonic, fetal) and why the Day 54 medication rules still stand. Tong 2008: after a normal scan with a heartbeat in 696 asymptomatic women, later miscarriage risk fell from 9.4% at 6 weeks to 0.5–0.7% at 9–10 weeks, with age and bleeding changing the numbers. Lacroix 2000: nausea in 74%, morning-only in 1.8%, peaking at 11–13 weeks, resolved in half by 14 weeks and 90% by 22. Red flags for hyperemesis, and why the FDA advises against home Dopplers.
action: Offer to keep a four-week sickness log on your phone so she doesn't have to: one line a day — nausea 0–10, number of vomits, fluids kept down yes/no. If it isn't easing by about 14 weeks (Day 98), or any red flag appears (no fluids kept down for a day, weight loss, dark or scant urine, dizziness on standing, blood in vomit), take the log to the practice.
